content:
Siri AI will debut next week with iOS 26, representing a major upgrade for the Apple assistant. Siri has many new features and improvements, but here are three examples that impressed me.

#1: Add NFL games to my calendar

It's American football season again, and every time the NFL schedule is released, I do a tedious but important task — adding the games to my calendar.

Sometimes the NFL provides .ics files that make it a bit easier, but doing this on a phone is still quite cumbersome, and usually doesn't include the information I want.

So this year I tried using Siri AI — it really saved me a lot of time.

I asked Siri to find all Dallas Cowboys games and add them to my calendar. Yes, I'm a fan of 'America's Team' — accept my condolences.

In my request I specified that Siri should include streaming platform information for each game. Now NFL games can be on FOX One, Paramount+, Peacock, Prime Video, ESPN, and even Netflix — there's really a lot to keep track of.

To my surprise, Siri did exactly what I wanted. All games were added to my calendar the way I wanted, complete with viewing information.

#2: Finding my license plate details

Just last week, I was filling out a form online that required my license plate number.

I didn't remember my plate number, and the car was with my wife at the time. But I was pretty sure there was a photo or some other record on my phone where I could find the plate.

I asked Siri: 'Can you find my current license plate number?'

Within seconds it found the answer. It gave me my plate number, along with a link to an email where Siri found that number. It turned out to be in a registration renewal email — I didn't even remember that email existed.

#3: Apple Watch band size

The Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 went on sale immediately after the September event earlier this week (you can pre-order here: Series 12, Ultra 4).

This year I chose the Apple Watch Series 12, and originally wanted a Braided Solo Loop band. I tried one a few years ago and really loved it.

Although I ultimately chose a different band, I did hit a snag when looking at the Solo Loop options: I couldn't remember my size.

Unlike other Apple Watch bands, the Solo Loop requires a very precise size to fit securely. I was in a rush when pre-ordering and didn't want to slow things down by having to try the size.

So I simply told Siri that I'd bought a Solo Loop before and wanted to find my size. It found the relevant information in a note I'd saved several years ago. Just like with the license plate, I had completely forgotten I'd written such a memo.

Siri AI summary

Siri can do far more than the few things I mentioned above. For example, I use it often to ask world-knowledge questions that I used to ask ChatGPT or Google Gemini.

But these three use cases highlight a core advantage Siri now has: using your personal data intelligently and with a focus on privacy.

How has your experience been with Siri AI on iOS 26? Feel free to share in the comments section.
